2.7 The fact and time of any detainee’s refusal to sign a custody
record, when asked in accordance with this Code, must be
recorded.
 10
Note for guidance
2A The purpose of paragraph 2.6A is to protect those involved in
serious organised crime investigations or arrests of particularly
violent suspects when there is reliable information that those
arrested or their associates may threaten or cause harm to those
involved. In cases of doubt, an officer of inspector rank or above
should be consulted.

3. Initial action
(a) Detained persons - normal procedure

3.1 When a person is brought to a police station under arrest or
arrested at the station having gone there voluntarily, the custody
officer must make sure the person is told clearly about:
 (a) the following continuing rights, which may be exercised at any
stage during the period in custody:
(i) their right to have someone informed of their arrest
as in section 5;
(ii) their right to consult privately with a solicitor and
that free independent legal advice is available;
(iii) their right to consult these Codes of Practice (see
Note 3D).
(iv) if applicable, their right to interpretation and
translation, see paragraph 3.7 , and the right to
communicate with their High Commission, Embassy
or Consulate, see paragraph 3.7A.
(b) their right to be informed about the offence and (as the case
may be), any further offences for which they are arrested whilst in
custody, and why they have been arrested and detained in
accordance with paragraphs 2.4, 3.4(a) and 11.1A of this Code and
paragraph 3.3 of Code G.
